newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cotton crops progress normally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cotton crops progress normally.

text.p: Heavy rain limited fieldwork on cotton crops in some U.S. states in the week ended June 8, National Agricultural Statistics Service said.
However, planting and crop development progressed on schedule, according to weekly crop reports from state agricultural statistics services.

MISSISSIPPI - According to the Mississippi Agricultural Statistics Service, there were two days suitable for fieldwork for the week ending June 8. Farming activities for the week were limited in some areas and stopped completely in others, due to continued rainfall. Soil moisture conditions were rated 1 percent short, 41 pct adequate and 58 pct surplus.
Cotton was 100 percent planted versus 100 pct a week ago, 100 pct a year ago, and 99 pct on a 5-year average. Crops were 98 pct emerged vs 97 pct last week, 100 pct last year and 97 pct on average.
Conditions were rated 7 pct excellent, 52 pct good, 31 pct fair, 8 pct poor and 2 pct very poor.

GEORGIA - Another week of unprecedented cool temperatures and cloudy damp weather slowed some crop development, according to the Georgia Agricultural Statistics Service (GASS). Rainfall was light except for a few local areas that were hit with heavy rains and storms that damaged crops. Cotton planting, despite less than ideal conditions, progressed normally. Warmer weather is needed for the state's cotton crops, GASS said.
Cotton was 96 percent planted versus 91 pct last week, 96 pct last year, and 96 pct on a five year average. Crops were 10 pct squared versus 5 pct last week, 24 pct last year and 23 pct on average.
Crop conditions were rated 4 pct excellent, 49 pct good, 39 pct fair, 7 pct poor and 1 pct very poor.

LOUISIANA - There were 4.7 suitable days for planting last week. Soil moisture was 6 percent short, 74 pct adequate and 20 pct surplus. Cotton was 100 percent planted versus 100 pct last year and a five year average of 100 pct.

Crops were 100 percent emerged versus 96 pct last week, 100 pct last year and an average of 99 pct. Crops were rated 1 percent excellent, 66 pct good, 30 pct fair and 3 pct poor. Squaring was 8 percent versus 17 pct last year and 23 pct average.

TEXAS - Rain early in the week gave way to much-needed sun by mid-week. Planting continued in the Plains with early fields showing good growth as temperatures rose during the week. Fields responded favorably to warmer temperatures in Central, Southern and coastal areas. Plants in the Valley were setting bolls. Statewide cotton condition was rated at 78 percent of normal compared with 58 pct last year.

The 1997 cotton crop was 83 percent planted versus 73 pct last week, 65 pct last year, and a five year average of 77 pct. Squaring was rated at 11 percent versus 13 pct last year, and 15 pct according to a five-year average.
Conditions were rated at 15 percent excellent, 47 pct good, 28 pct fair, 9 pct poor and 1 pct very poor.

CALIFORNIA - Field activities progressed normally in most areas despite light rainfall around midweek, in the northern two-thirds of the state. Cotton was cultivated, irrigated, weeded and sprayed for aphids, lygus and mites.

ARIZONA - Cotton development remained ahead of last year and the five-year average. Thirteen percent of the crop was setting bolls compared to 9 pct last year and 5 pct average. Crop conditions rated 1 percent very poor, 1 pct poor, 9 pct fair, 57 pct good and 32 pct excellent.
